userStories.title: Create SavedSkill Pydantic data model

userStories.title: Integrate skills into agent invocation
userStories.description: As a user, I want my enabled skills to be automatically available to the agent when I chat, so the agent can discover and use relevant skills.
acceptanceCriteria: Add `prepare_skill_files()` function in `backend/src/agents/__init__.py` following `prepare_memory_files()` pattern at lines 73-107
Function fetches enabled skills via `SkillService.search_enabled()`
Creates files map: `{"/skills/<name>/SKILL.md": create_file_data(skill.to_skill_md())}` for each enabled skill
Returns `(files_map, ["/skills/"])` when skills exist, or `({}, None)` when no enabled skills

In `backend/src/controllers/llm.py` `llm_invoke()`: call `prepare_skill_files()`, merge skill files as base layer `{**skill_files, **memory_files, **existing_files}`, pass skill sources to `construct_agent(skills=...)`
In `backend/src/utils/stream.py` `stream_generator()`: call `prepare_skill_files()`, merge skill files as base layer before memory files, pass skill sources to `construct_agent(skills=...)`
Agent works normally when no skills are enabled (empty files, None sources)
Typecheck passes (`make format`)
userStories.notes: The `skills` parameter is already supported by `create_deep_agent()` and threaded through `init_graph()` and `construct_agent()`. Just need to add the prepare function and wire it in the two entry points (llm_invoke and stream_generator). Skill files are the base layer — memory files override, then user files override both: `{**skill_files, **memory_files, **user_files}`.

userStories.title: Fix: Add SkillProvider to React provider tree
userStories.description: As a user, I need the /skills page to render without crashing. The SkillProvider context was never added to the provider tree in main.tsx, causing useSkillContext() to return an empty object and crash with 'useEffectGetSkills2 is not a function'.
acceptanceCriteria: Edit `frontend/src/main.tsx` — import `SkillProvider` from `./context/SkillContext`
Wrap `<SkillProvider>` around `<ProjectProvider>` inside `<AgentProvider>` in the provider chain
Navigate to http://localhost:5173/skills — page renders with Skills title, search bar, and empty state (no white screen)
No console errors related to `useEffectGetSkills` or `SkillContext`
Navigate to http://localhost:5173/skills/create — create page renders with Editor/Settings tabs
Typecheck passes
Verify in browser using agent-browser skill
userStories.notes: ROOT CAUSE: SkillProvider was defined in context/SkillContext.tsx but never imported/wrapped in main.tsx. The useSkillContext() hook returned the default empty createContext({}) value, so destructured methods like useEffectGetSkills were undefined. FIX: Add SkillProvider between AgentProvider and ProjectProvider in main.tsx provider chain.

userStories.title: Separate skills parameter from memory parameter
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the skills parameter separated from memory in the agent construction chain so DeepAgent uses SkillsMiddleware for progressive disclosure instead of loading skills as flat memory.
acceptanceCriteria: Add `skills: list[str] | None = None` parameter to `init_graph()`, `construct_agent()`, `Orchestra.__init__()`
Thread `skills=skills` through the chain: `Orchestra.__init__` -> `init_graph()` -> `create_deep_agent()`
In `llm_invoke()`: pass `memory=memory_sources, skills=skill_sources` (not combined)
In `stream_generator()`: same separation of memory and skills parameters
Typecheck/lint passes (`make format`)
userStories.notes: Currently skills and memory are combined as `memory=(skill_sources or []) + (memory_sources or []) or None`. Separate them so create_deep_agent() receives skills via its dedicated `skills` parameter for proper progressive disclosure via SkillsMiddleware.
